source.basis: Operator facility page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
Expedient Milwaukee publishes 1.6 MW of IT capacity across 27,000 square feet of technical space. At 10 kW per rack, a common density for mixed enterprise workloads, that is roughly 160 racks; at 40 kW per rack, a density associated with GPU-dense AI training, the same 1.6 MW supports only about 40 racks. Those are assumptions, not the operator's claims. The facility is small by the standards of AI infrastructure, where a single large training cluster can absorb tens of megawatts on its own.

PCI DSS qualifies the campus to host payment-card data under that standard's requirements. HIPAA qualifies it to host protected health information under federal rules. HITRUST adds a third-party audited control framework that satisfies many healthcare and financial customers. Taken together, the certifications describe a facility built for regulated enterprise data, not for the high-density, power-hungry workloads that drive frontier AI training.

Wisconsin has six data center facilities mapped in this site's dataset, but only one, this campus, has published a megawatt figure, so the 1.6 MW here represents 100 percent of the state's published capacity by default, a ceiling that reflects data scarcity more than genuine market size. That figure makes Expedient Milwaukee the ranked-first facility in the state by published IT load, though the ranking is nearly meaningless given that five other facilities publish nothing. For AI scaling decisions, where binding constraints run to hundreds of megawatts, this campus is a negligible quantity.
